issues.quote: It stopped with its master. I say that as a friend and not as a physician.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no reading or stopping time for the atelier regulator, and says nothing about any clock stopping at the time of death.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as a clock that stopped at the moment of death, and so treat the regulator's stopping as a fixed time anchor for the death or for the doctor's whereabouts.

issues.quote: A blow to the back of the head, struck from behind. It was a heavy blow, and I would say death was very quick. He would not have known much about it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information on how long death took, only the three clock facts.
issues.misreading: 'Very quick' could be read as death following the blow almost at once, which implies a duration and a time of death tied to the blow's timing.

issues.quote: I went out to the hall to fetch my cigar case from my coat.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says he went out to fetch the cigar case and does not say how long he was away.
issues.misreading: Later he says 'I was looking for my cigars', which suggests a search, and so a longer absence than the sheet gives. A solver could read the absence as lasting longer than the sheet allows.

issues.quote: She plays Chopin when she is thinking about something she will not discuss. I did not listen closely.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that Madame began playing as he went out and stopped when he came back.
issues.misreading: 'I did not listen closely' could be read as a doubt about whether the piano playing ran continuously while he was out, or whether she stopped at some other point.
